item.title: NEW: BYOD Ransomware Group Claims Breach of Michigan State University
item.description:
Headline: BYOD Ransomware Group Claims Breach of Michigan State University

Summary:
The 'BYOD' ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a major data breach at Michigan State University (MSU), alleging the exfiltration of 1.03 million records containing personal identifiable information (PII) and passwords for current and former students and staff. The group publicly stated that the university's incident response team failed to maintain communication after an initial contact, leading the attackers to leak the data.

Severity: High

Categories: Ransomware, Data Breach, Threat Actor

Meta Description: The 'BYOD' ransomware group claims a major data breach at Michigan State University, alleging the theft of 1.03 million records of students and staff.

item.title: NEW: Critical UnrealIRCd Flaw (CVE-2026-114713) Actively Exploited
item.description:
Headline: Critical UnrealIRCd Flaw (CVE-2026-114713) Actively Exploited

Summary:
A critical vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 with a CVSS score of 8.6, is being actively exploited in the wild just one day after a patch was released. The flaw allows for command execution with server privileges. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to apply the patch by November 16, 2026.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Cyberattack

Meta Description: A critical vulnerability in UnrealIRCd (CVE-2026-114713) is under active exploitation, allowing command execution. CISA has added it to the KEV list.

Headline: Kroll Report: 69% of Organizations Breached in Past Year

Summary:
Kroll's 2026 Data Breach Outlook report reveals a troubling landscape, with 69% of global organizations experiencing a data breach in the past year and 34% suffering more than one. The financial services industry was the most affected sector, accounting for 20% of breaches handled by Kroll. A key finding highlights the immense impact of supply chain risk, with 69% of all affected individuals being impacted by a breach at a third-party provider, often in the technology sector.

item.title: NEW: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures
item.description:
Headline: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures

Summary:
Google's Project Zero, an elite vulnerability research team, has announced a significant change to its disclosure policy. Effective immediately, the team is eliminating the 30-day grace period previously granted for patch adoption. Under the new "Full X" policy, technical details of a vulnerability will be made public 90 days after reporting to a vendor, regardless of whether a fix is available. The deadline will be progressively shortened to 30 days by 2028 to pressure vendors into faster patching cycles.

Severity: Informational

Categories: Policy and Compliance, Vulnerability, Patch Management

Meta Description: Google's Project Zero is implementing a stricter 'Full X' vulnerability disclosure policy, removing the 30-day grace period for patch adoption to close the patch gap.

Article Slug: google-project-zero-ends-30-day-grace-period-for-vulnerability-disclosure

item.title: NEW: Check Point Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Destructive ESXi Wipers
item.description:
Headline: Check Point Zero-Day Exploited to Deploy Destructive ESXi Wipers

Summary:
A critical zero-day vulnerability in Check Point's Gaia OS, CVE-2026-123039, is being actively exploited in the wild. Attackers are chaining an initial access vulnerability with this local privilege escalation flaw to gain root on security gateways. Once compromised, the gateways are used as a pivot point to deploy destructive wiper malware on VMware ESXi servers, impacting dozens of organizations and prompting CISA to add the flaw to its KEV catalog.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Cyberattack, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: A critical zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2026-123039) in Check Point's Gaia OS is actively exploited to gain root access and deploy destructive wiper malware on VMware ESXi servers.

item.title: NEW: Stolen AI Key at Fireworks AI Triggers Supply Chain Attack on Cursor
item.description:
Headline: Stolen AI Key at Fireworks AI Triggers Supply Chain Attack on Cursor

Summary:
A sophisticated supply chain attack began with a stolen API key from AI provider Fireworks AI, allowing attackers to breach developer tool company Cursor. The threat actors then injected a trojanized version of the popular 'Claude Code' VS Code extension into Cursor's marketplace. For 11 hours, approximately 5,000 developers downloaded the malicious extension, which installed a persistent SSH backdoor on their systems, highlighting the cascading risks in AI-powered development workflows.

Severity: High

Categories: Supply Chain Attack, Malware, Data Breach

Article Type: NewsArticle

Meta Description: A cascading supply chain attack originating from a breach at Fireworks AI led to the distribution of a trojanized VS Code extension with a backdoor via the Cursor developer platform.

item.description:
Headline: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old RCE Bug

Summary:
The PostgreSQL project has issued a significant minor version update that remediates 52 vulnerabilities. Most notably, the patch addresses a critical, 22-year-old remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability. Although the flaw requires authentication to exploit, it poses a substantial risk in many environments where credentials may be compromised. The discovery highlights the persistent danger of legacy bugs in mature, widely-trusted open-source projects and reinforces the need for diligent patch management.

item.description:
Headline: UnrealIRCd Command Injection Flaw Added to CISA KEV Catalog

Summary:
The U.S. CISA has added a critical command injection vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server, CVE-2026-114713, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The flaw, which stems from improper neutralization of delimiters, is confirmed to be under active exploitation. It allows attackers to inject and execute commands on vulnerable servers, posing a significant risk to organizations using the popular open-source IRC daemon. Federal agencies are now mandated to patch the vulnerability.
